data.prompt:
You are in an **Archon Horizon** workspace at `.`.

Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

Before modifying files, inspect the required and conversational inbox lanes:
`"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json`
then `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json`.
Protections are standing constraints even when already read. Address or explicitly
acknowledge unread conversations before ordinary advisory inbox material.

# Task
Task: pic-g
Title: Pic rep lane G: close Pic representability, no new hypotheses
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
References: roadmap=AJCR.jacobian,AJCR.w4-rep; inbox=I-0838

Pic representability should close, and closing it is your objective — pick a roadmap item and make major progress on it, USING NO ADDITIONAL HYPOTHESIS (`rep` has 93 consumers and 0 producers; last round added 71 more consumers and the headline did not move). Your work must be directly usable by Pic representability and the other items, not local to your row. Be ambitious: don't scope down because something is large or missing from mathlib — building substrate and huge refactoring are licensed. Delete unfaithful roadmap items and create truer ones, but never a row another lane owns at HEAD. Collaborate with the other lanes; announce what you take before you start.

YOUR PEERS this round are pic-a, pic-b, pic-c, pic-d, pic-e, pic-f, pic-g, pic-h — eight provers, no reviewer. Four work Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge (pic-a, pic-b, pic-e, pic-f) and four work Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild (pic-c, pic-d, pic-g, pic-h). With eight lanes on one ledger, announcing what you take BEFORE you start is what stops two lanes proving the same lemma — read the inbox for what the others announced, and say so if you are taking something already held.

This is a headless, one-shot session: advance the REAL objective, commit each
verified unit and any final edits, keep operational comments to the delta,
then write the skill's brief final report.

data.content:
1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.
355

=== I-1482 ===
[persistent] SUPERSEDES I-0838 AND I-0839 ENTIRELY (2026-07-30). Both describe the previous round and are now WRONG about who is alive. Do not follow their lane lists.

THE ROUND THAT IS ACTUALLY RUNNING. Eight prover lanes, NO reviewer:
  Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge:         pic-a, pic-b, pic-e, pic-f
  Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild: pic-c, pic-d, pic-g, pic-h
Every lane from the previous round (review-ajc, review-ajcr, ajc-p1..p4, ajcr-p1..p4) is DEAD. I killed them.

OWNERSHIP, corrected. I verified at 2026-07-30 11:30 that ZERO roadmap items carry an owner: the dead lanes released their claims. So no --owner field fences you off from anything right now. An --owner value is a live claim ONLY if it is one of the eight lanes above. Any other owner value is a corpse - clear it and take the row.

THERE ARE NO RANKS THIS ROUND. I-0838 ranked provers p1..p4 by "most important". That is gone: all eight lanes have the same objective and choose freely. Announce what you take in the inbox BEFORE you start, and read what the others announced - with eight writers on one ledger that announcement is the only thing stopping two lanes proving the same lemma. If you find your target already announced, take something else and say so.

WHAT I-0838 STILL GETS RIGHT, and it is the reason I am not simply archiving it: the fresh-private-index commit discipline, and the bar (sorry-free is necessary not sufficient; exhibit a witness for every antecedent or name which one stays open; never introduce a class whose statement does not mention its object; never discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed). Those still bind. Read I-0838 for that content only, not for the lane roster.

I-0491 AND I-0492 REMAIN BINDING AND UNCHANGED. Read them before touching the seam.
=== I-0838 ===
[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 — the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.

WHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.

THE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT
- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` — reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.
- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` — takes the MOST important open representability item.
- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` — 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where "important" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.

CLAIMING — do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.
 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.
 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.
 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.
 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body "CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> — <one line on what discharging it buys>"`.
 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.

RANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap — rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.

YOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body "…"`. 1	/-

4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZero
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap
8	
9	/-!
10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
11	
12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
33	-/
34	
35	set_option autoImplicit false
36	
37	universe u
38	
39	open CategoryTheory
40	
41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
42	
43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
45	
46	noncomputable section
47	
48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
49	
50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
57	
58	section DegAt
59	
60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
61	
62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
63	@[simp]
64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
67	
68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
75	
76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
81	  rfl
82	
83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
92	
93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
98	
99	end DegAt
100	
101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
102	
103	variable (C) in
104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
109	    degAt lam t = 0}
110	  one_mem' := by
111	    intro K _ _ t
112	    exact degAt_one t
113	  mul_mem' := by
114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
116	  inv_mem' := by
117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
119	
120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
125	  Iff.rfl
126	
127	variable (C) in
128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
131	points. -/
132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
136	
137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
139	@[simp]
140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
143	  rfl
144	
145	variable (C) in
146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
150	functor. -/
151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
154	  map_id T := by
155	    ext lam U
156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
157	  map_comp g h := by
158	    ext lam U
159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
160	
161	@[simp]
162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
164	  rfl
165	
166	@[simp]
167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
170	  rfl
171	
172	variable (C) in
173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/
176	def pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
177	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype
178	  naturality _ _ _ := rfl
179	
180	end
181	
182	end AlgebraicGeometry

Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic
import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Pullbacks

/-!
# The relative Picard functor of a curve

For a scheme `C` over a field `k` (an object of `Over (Spec k)`) this file defines the
relative Picard functor of Grothendieck–Kleiman:
$$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(T) \;=\; \operatorname{Pic}(C \times_k T)\,/\,
  \operatorname{Pic}(T),$$
line-bundle classes on `C ⊗ T` modulo classes pulled back from the test object `T`
along the second projection. The quotient — never the absolute `Pic(C ⊗ T)`, which is
not even a separated presheaf in any useful sense — is the functor that étale
sheafification and the representability theorem consume.

Products are the cartesian-monoidal product of `Over (Spec k)` (chosen pullbacks of
schemes): `C ⊗ T`, projection `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`, matching the vocabulary
of the challenge statement file.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase C T`: the subgroup of `(C ⊗ T).left.CechPic` of classes
  pulled back from `T` along the second projection.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPic C T`: the relative Picard group, the quotient by
  `picFromBase C T`, a `CommGroup`; `relPicMk` is the projection, with
  `relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff` the exact coset relation (a genuine range condition, no
  choice, no `Nonempty (≅)`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMap C g`: restriction along `g : T' ⟶ T`, descended from
  pullback of Čech classes along `C ◁ g`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicFunctor C`: the relative Picard functor
  `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
open AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme (CechPic)

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

noncomputable section

/-- The subgroup of Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` pulled back from the test object `T`
along the second projection. The relative Picard group is the quotient by it. -/
def picFromBase (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup ((C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :=
  (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range

lemma mem_picFromBase_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
    L ∈ picFromBase C T ↔ ∃ N : T.left.CechPic, CechPic.map (snd C T).left N = L :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: Picard classes on `C ⊗ T`
modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ picFromBase C T

noncomputable instance (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : CommGroup (relPic C T) :=
  QuotientGroup.Quotient.commGroup (picFromBase C T)

/-- The projection from Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` to the relative Picard group. -/
noncomputable def relPicMk (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic →* relPic C T :=
  QuotientGroup.mk' (picFromBase C T)

lemma relPicMk_surjective (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    Function.Surjective (relPicMk C T) :=
  QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective (picFromBase C T)

/-- The exact coset relation: two Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` have equal image in the
relative Picard group iff their ratio is pulled back from `T`. -/
lemma relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    {L L' : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
    relPicMk C T L = relPicMk C T L' ↔ L / L' ∈ picFromBase C T :=
  QuotientGroup.eq_iff_div_mem

@[elab_as_elim]
theorem relPic.ind {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {motive : relPic C T → Prop}
    (mk : ∀ L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic, motive (relPicMk C T L)) (x : relPic C T) :
    motive x :=
  QuotientGroup.induction_on x mk

variable {T T' T'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}

/-- Pullback of Čech Picard classes along `C ◁ g` sends classes from `T` to classes
from `T'`: the well-definedness of `relPicMap` on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
lemma picFromBase_le_comap (g : T' ⟶ T) :
    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C T').comap (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) := by
  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩
  refine ⟨CechPic.map g.left N, ?_⟩
  show CechPic.map (snd C T').left (CechPic.map g.left N)
      = CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left (CechPic.map (snd C T).left N)
  rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
    ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left, ← Over.comp_left, whiskerLeft_snd]

/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along `g : T' ⟶ T`: pull back along
`C ◁ g` and descend to the quotients. -/
noncomputable def relPicMap (g : T' ⟶ T) : relPic C T →* relPic C T' :=
  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C T')
    (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) (picFromBase_le_comap C g)

@[simp]
lemma relPicMap_mk (g : T' ⟶ T) (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
    relPicMap C g (relPicMk C T L) = relPicMk C T' (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left L) :=
  QuotientGroup.map_mk' _ _ _ _ L

lemma relPicMap_id (x : relPic C T) : relPicMap C (𝟙 T) x = x := by
  induction x using relPic.ind with
  | mk L =>
    rw [relPicMap_mk, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id, Over.id_left,
      Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
    rfl

7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtUnit

9	/-!
10	# THE `∀ T` BINDER OF THE `pic⁰` VANISHING IS A STATEMENT ABOUT TEST RINGS
11	
12	Two independent routes to a producer of `(pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy` meet at one
13	hypothesis, and that hypothesis has **no producer** anywhere in the project:
14	
15	  `hvan : ∀ S : Over (Spec k), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C S)`
16	
17	* `Pic0VanishingRoute.jacobianData_of_subsingleton` consumes it and returns a `JacobianData C`
18	  with no atlas, no chart certificate, no coverage and no divisor representability;
19	* `Pic0ChartSeamPairDecided.isLocallySurjective_abelSigmaChartZero_iff` proves the seam's
20	  *coverage* antecedent at parameter `0` is **equivalent** to it.
21	
22	So `hvan` is not one route's private input; it is where the two routes' costs coincide.
23	
24	**What this file does.** It replaces the `∀ T` quantifier — over all objects of
25	`Over (Spec k)`, i.e. over all `k`-schemes — by a quantifier over commutative `k`-algebras,
26	and it proves the replacement is an **equivalence**, not a sufficient condition.
27	
28	## Why the landed reduction does not already do this
29	
30	`Pic0VanishingRoute` reduces the quantifier for `picEt` (`subsingleton_picEt_of_affine`) and
31	proves that one is an equivalence (`subsingleton_picEtAff_of_forall`).  Its degree-zero
32	consequence `subsingleton_pic0_of_affine` runs **one way only**, and its own docstring says
33	why that is not a repair: the hypothesis is vanishing of the whole `picEt`, which is *strictly
34	stronger* and false at any curve carrying a class of nonzero degree — including `ℙ¹`, where
35	`pic⁰` does vanish.  So the landed chain cannot be applied to the hypothesis anyone needs, in
36	either direction.  The reduction here is for `pic0Subgroup` directly and never mentions
37	`picEt` vanishing.
38	
39	## The mechanism, and why it needed no new mathematics
40	
41	Separation, not gluing.  `Subsingleton` is an equality statement, so only the *ext* half of
42	the descent is used: the affine opens of `T.left` give a morphism-form open cover of `T` by
43	the affine-open test objects `Over.fromSpecAffine T U : overSpec k Γ(T.left, U) ⟶ T`
44	(`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:60`), each an open immersion on the left because
45	`IsAffineOpen.fromSpec` is; and `pic0Subgroup_ext_of_cover`
46	(`Picard/PicEtCoverBridge.lean:342`) says two degree-zero classes agreeing on every member
47	agree.  Under the affine hypothesis each pair of restrictions agrees for free.
48	
49	The `∃!`-gluing bridge in the same file (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`) is *not* used:
50	producing a class from local data would need the compatibility datum, and a subsingleton
51	statement never has to produce anything.  That asymmetry is the whole reason this is cheap
52	where the corresponding representability statement is not.
53	
54	## What the reduced hypothesis is, exactly
55	
56	Three equivalent spellings are given, each strictly more ring-level than the last:
57	
58	1. `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))` at every `k`-algebra `A` — the direct form;
59	2. the same transported through `picEtAffineEquiv` to a separation statement about **plus
60	   classes** `PicEtAff C A` of the test algebra, with the degree condition read through the
61	   comparison;
62	3. with the field points of `overSpec k A` themselves ring-level: every
63	   `t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A` **is** `Over.overSpecMap φ` for an algebra map
64	   `φ : A →ₐ[k] K` (`exists_algHom_eq_of_overSpec_hom`, `Spec.preimage` plus the tower
65	   identity).  So the surviving quantifier in (2) ranges over algebra maps into fields, and no
66	   scheme, open, or morphism of schemes occurs in the hypothesis at all.
67	
68	## What this does NOT do
69	
70	* **It does not prove the vanishing, at any curve.**  It moves the quantifier; the
71	  mathematical content — a computation of the degree-zero relative Picard group of the curve
72	  over an arbitrary test *ring* — is untouched and remains unproduced.  In particular nothing
73	  here discharges `hvan` at `ℙ¹`, where `Curve/P1Curve.lean` supplies the three curve binders
74	  and `Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` gives `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0`.
75	* **It does not make the hypothesis cheap.**  `infer_instance` fails on
76	  `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))` (measured), so the reduced form has content;
77	  the reduction is a change of coordinates on a real obligation, not a discount.
78	* **It says nothing about the atlas route's own residue.**  The coverage clause at
79	  parameter `n > 0` is blocked on a spreading-out (`Pic0ChartCoverageSlice.lean:221-228`),
80	  which is a different obligation and is not addressed here.
81	
82	## Main declarations
83	
84	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_test_mem` — the affine opens of a test give a
85	  morphism-form open cover of it by affine test objects.
86	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_overSpec` — **the reduction**: vanishing at
87	  every affine test gives vanishing at every test.
88	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall` — **the converse**, so the
89	  two are the same hypothesis.
90	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_forall_iff_overSpec` — the equivalence, bundled.
91	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_algHom_eq_of_overSpec_hom` — every field point of an affine test is
92	  `Spec` of an algebra map, so the field-point quantifier is ring-level too.
93	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_picEtAff_sep` — the reduced hypothesis in
94	  plus-class coordinates.
95	* `AlgebraicGeometry.jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` — **the producer**, with the
96	  quantifier already reduced: a `JacobianData C` from vanishing at affine tests only.
97	-/
98	
99	set_option autoImplicit false
100	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
101	
102	universe u
103	
104	open CategoryTheory Opposite
105	
106	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
107	
108	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
109	
110	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
111	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
112	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
113	
114	noncomputable section
115	
116	/-! ## The affine-open cover of a test object -/
117	
118	/-- The affine-open test object of an affine open is an open immersion on the left, because
119	`IsAffineOpen.fromSpec` is.  Stated as an instance so that the cover lemmas of
120	`PicEtCoverBridge` apply to the family `Over.fromSpecAffine T` without a local `haveI`. -/
121	instance isOpenImmersion_fromSpecAffine_left (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
122	    (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
123	    IsOpenImmersion (AlgebraicGeometry.Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left :=
124	  U.2.isOpenImmersion_fromSpec
125	
126	/-- **The affine opens of a test object cover it, in morphism form**: every point of `T.left`
127	is in the range of `Over.fromSpecAffine T U` for some affine open `U`.
128	
129	This is the `hcov` hypothesis of the `PicEtCoverBridge` cover lemmas, at the one cover every
130	test object has: the affine opens form a basis, and the range of
131	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U` is `U` itself (`IsAffineOpen.range_fromSpec`). -/
132	theorem exists_affineOpen_test_mem (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (p : T.left) :
133	    ∃ U : T.left.affineOpens,
134	      p ∈ (AlgebraicGeometry.Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.opensRange := by
135	  obtain ⟨U, hU, hmem, -⟩ :=
136	    (TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp T.left.isBasis_affineOpens)
137	      (show p ∈ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) from trivial)
138	  refine ⟨⟨U, hU⟩, ?_⟩
139	  have hrange : Set.range (AlgebraicGeometry.Over.fromSpecAffine T ⟨U, hU⟩).left.base
140	      = ((⟨U, hU⟩ : T.left.affineOpens).1 : Set T.left) := by
141	    change Set.range (hU.fromSpec).base = _
142	    exact hU.range_fromSpec
143	  change p ∈ Set.range (AlgebraicGeometry.Over.fromSpecAffine T ⟨U, hU⟩).left.base
144	  rw [hrange]
145	  exact hmem
146	
147	/-! ## The reduction of the `∀ T` binder -/
148	
149	/-- **THE REDUCTION**: if `pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)` is a subsingleton at every
150	commutative `k`-algebra `A`, then `pic0Subgroup C T` is a subsingleton at every test object
151	`T` — over an arbitrary base field, with no finiteness, affineness or quasi-compactness
152	hypothesis on `T`.
153	
154	Only the *separation* half of Zariski descent is used: two degree-zero classes agreeing on
155	every member of the affine-open cover agree (`pic0Subgroup_ext_of_cover`), and under the
156	hypothesis the restrictions to each member agree because the member's whole group is a
157	subsingleton.  Nothing is glued, so the compatibility datum that makes the corresponding
158	representability statement expensive never appears.
159	
160	Contrast `subsingleton_pic0_of_affine` (`Pic0VanishingRoute.lean:283`), whose hypothesis is
161	vanishing of the whole `picEt` at every test algebra: that implies this one but is strictly
162	stronger, and is false at any curve with a class of nonzero degree. -/
163	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_overSpec
164	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A],
165	      Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)))
166	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T) :=
167	  ⟨fun _ _ => pic0Subgroup_ext_of_cover
168	    (fun U : T.left.affineOpens => AlgebraicGeometry.Over.fromSpecAffine T U)
169	    (exists_affineOpen_test_mem T)
170	    fun U => @Subsingleton.elim _ (h Γ(T.left, U.1)) _ _⟩
171	
172	/-- **THE CONVERSE**, so the reduction is an equivalence and not a weakening: an affine test
173	is a test.
174	
175	Recorded because a quantifier reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its
176	conclusion relocates the gap instead of naming it — which is exactly the defect of the landed
177	`picEt`-mediated chain this file replaces. -/
178	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall
179	    (h : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T))
180	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
181	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) :=
182	  h (overSpec k A)
183	
184	/-- **The equivalence, bundled**: "the degree-zero relative Picard group vanishes at every
185	test object" and "it vanishes at every test ring" are the *same* hypothesis.
186	
187	This is the form to quote when pricing either route to a `rep` producer: the `∀ T` binder that
188	`I-1603` calls "the whole difficulty" is not itself the difficulty — the ring-level content
189	is. -/
190	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_forall_iff_overSpec :
191	    (∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T))
192	      ↔ ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A],
193	          Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) :=
194	  ⟨fun h A _ _ => subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall C h A,
195	    fun h => subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_overSpec C h⟩
196	
197	/-! ## The field-point quantifier is ring-level too -/
198	
199	/-- **Every field point of an affine test is `Spec` of an algebra map.**
200	
201	`pic0Subgroup` is cut out by degree vanishing at every field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`
202	(`Pic0Functor.lean:107`), which at a general test is a morphism of schemes.  At an affine test
203	it is not: `Spec.preimage` inverts `Spec.map` on morphisms between affine schemes, and the
204	triangle over `Spec k` becomes the scalar-tower identity `algebraMap k K = φ ∘ algebraMap k A`
205	by `Spec.map_injective`.
206	
207	Together with the reduction above, this is what makes the reduced hypothesis *entirely*
208	ring-level: no scheme, open, or morphism of schemes occurs in it. -/
209	theorem exists_algHom_eq_of_overSpec_hom (A K : Type u) [CommRing A] [Field K]
210	    [Algebra k A] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A) :
211	    ∃ phi : A →ₐ[k] K, t = Over.overSpecMap phi := by
212	  have hw : t.left ≫ (overSpec k A).hom = (overSpec k K).hom := Over.w t
213	  set psi : CommRingCat.of A ⟶ CommRingCat.of K := Spec.preimage t.left with hpsi
214	  have hmap : Spec.map psi = t.left := Spec.map_preimage t.left
215	  have htower : CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A) ≫ psi
216	      = CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K) := by
217	    apply Spec.map_injective
218	    rw [Spec.map_comp, hmap]
219	    exact hw
220	  have hcom : ∀ r : k, psi.hom (algebraMap k A r) = algebraMap k K r := fun r =>
221	    congrArg (fun f => f r) (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom htower)
222	  refine ⟨{ __ := psi.hom, commutes' := hcom }, ?_⟩
223	  ext : 1
224	  exact hmap.symm
225	
226	/-! ## The reduced hypothesis in plus-class coordinates -/
227	
228	/-- **The reduced hypothesis transported through the affine comparison**: a *separation*
229	statement about the plus classes `PicEtAff C A` of the test algebra.
230	
231	`picEtAffineEquiv` (`PicEt.lean:235`) is a group isomorphism `picEt C (overSpec k A) ≃*
232	PicEtAff C A`, so a degree-zero class of an affine test is a plus class of `A` whose
233	`degAt`-pullbacks vanish.  This is the spelling to attack: `PicEtAff C A` is the one-step étale
234	plus of the relative Picard group at a commutative ring, with no scheme-level machinery
235	between it and the hypothesis. -/
236	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_picEtAff_sep
237	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (q q' : PicEtAff C A),
238	      (∀ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : Algebra k K) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A),
239	        degAt ((picEtAffineEquiv C A).symm q) t = 0) →
240	      (∀ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : Algebra k K) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A),
241	        degAt ((picEtAffineEquiv C A).symm q') t = 0) →
242	      q = q')
243	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
244	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) := by
245	  refine ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext ?_⟩
246	  refine (picEtAffineEquiv C A).injective ?_
247	  refine h A (picEtAffineEquiv C A s.1) (picEtAffineEquiv C A t.1) ?_ ?_
248	  · intro K _ _ tt
249	    rw [MulEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
250	    exact s.2 K tt
251	  · intro K _ _ tt
252	    rw [MulEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
253	    exact t.2 K tt
254	
255	/-! ## The producer, with the quantifier already reduced -/
256	
257	/-- **`JacobianData C` from vanishing at affine tests only.**
258	
259	The composite of the reduction with `jacobianData_of_subsingleton`
260	(`Pic0VanishingRoute.lean`).  Its hypothesis mentions no test object: only the degree-zero
261	Picard group of the curve at a commutative `k`-algebra.
262	
263	This is the shape a lane computing `Pic⁰` over rings should target — and note what it does
264	*not* need: no atlas, no chart certificate, no coverage clause, no divisor representability,
265	no index finiteness, no rational point. -/
266	def jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton
267	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A],
268	      Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))) :
269	    JacobianData C :=
270	  jacobianData_of_subsingleton C (subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_overSpec C h)
271	
272	end
273	
274	end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsCocycle

/-!
# The definitional Picard group: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf

For a scheme `X`, this file defines the Picard group of record of this development:
the Čech cohomology `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site, computed on **pointed
covers** (one open per point of `X`, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsCocycle`) and
stabilized along the refinement preorder.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic`: the Picard group `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` as the quotient
  of `Σ 𝒰, X.unitsH1 𝒰` by agreement on a common refinement, with its `CommGroup`
  structure and the constructor/eliminator API `CechPic.mk`, `CechPic.ind`,
  `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff`, `CechPic.mk_unitsRes`, `CechPic.mk_mul_mk_inf`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.map`: contravariant functoriality — for
  `f : X ⟶ Y` the pullback `Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic` — with the strict functor laws
  `CechPic.map_id` and `CechPic.map_comp` (the lane keystone).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`: on a scheme with a
  subsingleton underlying space (e.g. `Spec` of a field) the Picard group is trivial.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Opposite CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme

variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}

/-! ## The Picard group  -/

instance cechPicSetoid (X : Scheme.{u}) : Setoid (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) where
  r p q := ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1),
    unitsRes h₁ p.2 = unitsRes h₂ q.2
  iseqv := by
    constructor
    · exact fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, le_rfl, le_rfl, rfl⟩
    · rintro p q ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
      exact ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, e.symm⟩
    · rintro p q r ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩
      refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_left.trans h₁, inf_le_right.trans h₄, ?_⟩
      have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
      have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
      simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
      exact e₁'.trans e₂'

/-- The definitional Picard group of a scheme: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf,
stabilized along refinement of pointed covers. -/
def CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
  Quotient (cechPicSetoid X)

namespace CechPic

/-- The Picard class of a unit Čech `H¹` class on a pointed cover. -/
def mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : X.CechPic :=
  ⟦⟨𝒰, a⟩⟧

@[elab_as_elim]
theorem ind {motive : X.CechPic → Prop}
    (mk : ∀ (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰), motive (mk 𝒰 a)) (x : X.CechPic) :
    motive x :=
  Quotient.ind (fun p ↦ by obtain ⟨𝒰, a⟩ := p; exact mk 𝒰 a) x

theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} {a : X.unitsH1 𝒰} {b : X.unitsH1 𝒱} :
    mk 𝒰 a = mk 𝒱 b ↔
      ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒱),
        unitsRes h₁ a = unitsRes h₂ b :=
  Quotient.eq

...

/-

import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.RigidEngineLatticeCoherence
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.RigidEngine2Nakayama
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.RigidEngine3Rigidity
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.AffineVanishingQcoh
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.TwoCover

/-!
# RE-4 — the sheaf-level assembly of the rigid engine (Layer 1, abstract)

This file assembles the module-algebra rigid engine (RE-1/2/3,
`informal/w4-rigid-engine-worksheet.md` §1.2 Level 2) at the sheaf level: for a sheaf `F`
of `R`-modules on the small Zariski site of a scheme `X`, packaged quasi-coherently on an
affine two-chart cover `U₀, U₁` (`Scheme.QcohOn`, w4-1), it constructs **the two-lattice
pair of `F`** and fires the engine on it.

* `Scheme.TwoCoverPairData` — the coordinate data of the cover: chart coordinates
  `g₀ ∈ Γ(X, U₀)`, `g₁ ∈ Γ(X, U₁)` with the overlap-as-basic-open identifications
  `U₀ ⊓ U₁ = D(g₀) = D(g₁)`, the `R`-linearity of their packaged actions, and the
  mutual-inverse law `g₀·g₁ = 1` on the overlap (expressed on the packaged actions:
  the two `qsmul` compositions are the identity of `F(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`).
* `Scheme.TwoCoverPairData.pair` — the two-lattice pair with carriers

/-!
# Base change of the two-term complex and of `H¹` on the relative curve

CBC-1/2 for the structure sheaf, bundled: for the curve bundle `C` over a field `k`, a
tower of test rings `R → R'` (commutative `k`-algebras) and the base-changed affine
two-cover `relCover C R D` of the relative curve `C_R`, this file base-changes the
two-term Čech complex `Γ(V₀ᴿ) × Γ(V₁ᴿ) → Γ(V₀ᴿ ⊓ V₁ᴿ)` along `R → R'` and deduces the
degree-one comparison isomorphism — Kleiman's "cohomology commutes with base change" in
the curve-lite two-cover form.

* `LinearMap.quotRangeBaseChangeEquiv` — the general right-exactness input: base change
  commutes with cokernels, `A ⊗[R] (N ⧸ range f) ≃ₗ[A] (A ⊗[R] N) ⧸ range (f.baseChange A)`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.relTermBaseChange` — **CBC-1, termwise**: for a qcqs open
  `V ⊆ C.left`, the `R'`-linear equivalence
  `R' ⊗[R] Γ(C_R, V_R) ≃ₗ[R'] Γ(C_{R'}, V_{R'})`, with the computation rule
  `relTermBaseChange_tmul` (`r' ⊗ y ↦ r' • relSectionsMap y`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.relDiffBaseChange` — **CBC-1, the complex**: the base change of the
  two-cover restriction-difference map `TwoCover.diff` over `R` is carried to the
  difference map over `R'` under the term equivalences (the commuting square).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.relH1CokBaseChange` — **CBC-2 (`i = 1`), cokernel form**:
  `R' ⊗[R] H1Cok R (C_R) ≃ₗ[R'] H1Cok R' (C_{R'})`, unconditionally in `R → R'` (the
  cokernel of a base-changed complex is the base change of the cokernel; no flatness).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.relH1BaseChange` — **CBC-2 (`i = 1`)**: the same statement on the
  cohomology carriers, `R' ⊗[R] H¹(C_R, 𝒪) ≃ₗ[R'] H¹(C_{R'}, 𝒪)`, through the landed
  relative two-cover identification `relTwoCoverH1`.

Degree zero for the structure sheaf needs no separate statement: `H⁰(C_R, 𝒪) ≃+* R`
on the nose (`AlgebraicGeometry.relStructureSectionsTop`), so its base change is
`R ⊗_R R' ≃ R'`.

## Implementation notes

The overlap opens `V₀ᴿ ⊓ V₁ᴿ` (the `TwoCover.H1Cok` spelling) and
`fst ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)` (the base-change spelling) are definitionally equal; statements
are given in the `H1Cok` spelling, and spelling adapters are introduced as local `have`s
justified by `exact` where the two must meet. See
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.RelativeSectionsLinear` for the transparency option.

/-
-/
import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.InvertibleLocalTrivialization
import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.LocalizationTrivialization
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CechPicToPic

/-!
# Surjectivity of the Čech–Picard descent homomorphism, and the dictionary

For an affine scheme `X` this file proves surjectivity of the descent homomorphism
`CechPic.toPic : X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)` and assembles the full
**Čech–Picard dictionary**

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.cechPicEquivPic : X.CechPic ≃* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`

— the isomorphism between the definitional Čech Picard group on pointed Zariski covers
and mathlib's Picard group of invertible modules (the TODO of
`Mathlib.RingTheory.PicardGroup`: "exhibit isomorphism with `H¹(Spec R, 𝓞ˣ)`").

The route: an invertible module `N` over `Γ(X, ⊤)` trivializes on the basic open of
some section outside every prime, so the trivializing sections span the unit ideal
(`Module.Invertible.span_tensor_free_eq_top`) and their basic opens cover `X`.  A
choice of one trivializing basic neighborhood per point is a `TrivializingFamily`; the
transition units of its trivializations (`Module.transitionUnit`) form a unit Čech
cocycle on the associated pointed cover.  Along any finite basic refinement the
restricted cover cocycle is the transition cocycle of the pushed-forward
trivializations, so its descended module is `N` itself
(`IsLocalization.AwayCover.picClass_trivializationCocycle`), and `toPic` hits the class
of `N`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
open TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme

variable {X : Scheme.{u}}

/-! ## Trivializing families -/

/-- A pointed trivializing family for a module `N` over the global sections of `X`: one
section per point, whose basic open contains the point and carries a trivialization of
the base change of `N`.  Invertible modules over affine schemes always admit one
(`TrivializingFamily.nonempty`). -/
structure TrivializingFamily (X : Scheme.{u}) (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N]
    [Module Γ(X, ⊤) N] : Type u where
  /-- The trivializing section at a point. -/
  sec : X → Γ(X, ⊤)
  /-- Each point lies in the basic open of its section. -/
  mem_basicOpen : ∀ x, x ∈ X.basicOpen (sec x)
  /-- The chosen trivialization of `N` over the basic open. -/
=== AlgebraicJacobian/Tangent/TwoChartCechPic.lean
/-

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RefinementInjectivity
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.AffineCech
import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.TruncExpCech

/-!
# The two-chart Čech `Ȟ¹` of units embeds in the Picard group (W5-T4 clause (iii-a)/(iii-b))

For a scheme `X` with two opens `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`, the two-chart Čech cohomology of units

```
Ȟ¹(V₀,V₁ ; 𝒪ˣ)  =  Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ ⧸ (im Γ(V₀)ˣ · im Γ(V₁)ˣ)
```

maps to the definitional Picard group `X.CechPic`, **injectively**
(`Scheme.twoChartClass_injective`). This file builds that map and proves the injectivity.

## Why this file exists: clauses (iii-a) and (iii-b), which are not about dual numbers

`informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` §6 splits the Wave-5 residue "clause (iii)" — the last input to
the Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11 dimension identity — into three parts, and observes that **two of
them contain no dual numbers, no curves and no `H¹`**. Those two are exactly this file:

* **(iii-a)** the comparison homomorphism `twoChartClass` exists;
* **(iii-b)** it is injective.

Both are general statements about a scheme with a two-open cover, so they are stated here at
that generality rather than at `C ×_k Spec k[ε]`. The remaining part, **(iii-c)**
(surjectivity onto the `ε`-kernel), is the only one that needs the thickening; it consumes
`DualNumber.free_of_cyclic_mod_eps` and lives elsewhere.

The two-chart Čech quotient here is the **same carrier** the truncated-exponential engine of
`Tangent/TruncExpCech.lean` computes: `TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits` of the two restriction
maps. So `twoChartClass` is precisely the arrow that connects the (landed) T2 engine to the
(definitional) Picard group, in the direction the tangent computation needs.

## Implementation notes

`CechPic` is built on **pointed** covers — one open per point — so a two-open cover enters
through a selector `sel : X → Bool` with `x ∈ V (sel x)`, exactly as
`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.pieceIndex` and `thetaFieldChartIndex` do elsewhere in the tree.
Indexing the charts by `Bool` (rather than by two named opens) is what makes the cocycle law a
`cases`-bash that closes uniformly.

The cocycle attached to an overlap unit `u` has pair values `1` on the diagonal, `u` at
`(0,1)` and the `inf_comm`-transport of `u⁻¹` at `(1,0)` (`Scheme.twoChartPairUnit`).

**A negative result, recorded so it is not retried** (worksheet §6.2): the slick spelling
`pairUnit s t = u ^ (δ t − δ s)`, which would close the cocycle law by `zpow_add` alone, does
**not** typecheck. On the diagonal the ambient open `T` need only be `≤ V s`, where `u` — a
section on `V₀ ⊓ V₁` — cannot be restricted at all. The exponent trick needs a unit on the
union and there is none. The eight-case `cases` bash is the honest route, and it is three
lines.

## Main declarations

/-!
# (iii-c2-Zar): chart-trivial classes are representable on the two-chart cover (W5-T4)

The **Zariski half** of clause `(iii-c2)` (`informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` §6.9). For a scheme
`X` with two opens `V : Bool → X.Opens` covering it:

> `Scheme.twoChartClassHom_surjOn_of_chartTrivial` —
> if `L : X.CechPic` restricts trivially to each chart (`CechPic.map (V s).ι L = 1`), then
> `L = twoChartClassHom V sel hmem u` for an overlap unit `u : Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ`.

Composed with the landed `(iii-c1)` normalization this is the whole cohomological content of
`(iii-c2)`: **no `IsAffine`, no dual numbers, no curve hypothesis.** Everything geometric in
the T4 lane is thereby confined to the single remaining clause `(iii-c2-aff)`, "an `ε`-kernel
class is trivial on each *thickened* chart", for which `Picard/EffectivityMoving.lean` is the
correct tool (see the retraction in §6.9 — that file bridges *into* chart triviality, so it
belongs to `(iii-c2-aff)`, not here).

74	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field` — **non-vacuity at a real
75	  curve**: the same at `P1.asOver k` with *no hypothesis at all*, since
76	  `Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` supplies `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0` over an arbitrary field.
77	
78	Both are stated with **three** curve binders: `GeometricallyReduced` is unused in each
79	(measured — the linter reports it), even though the surrounding `picEt` descent material
80	carries four.
81	-/
82	
83	set_option autoImplicit false
84	
85	universe u
86	
87	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
88	
89	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
90	
91	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
92	variable [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
93	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
94	
95	-- Carries the base-change instance stack of the field layer through the plus quotient's
96	-- cover-refinement calculus; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap precedent.
97	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
98	/-- **A plus class of degree zero over a field test is trivial, at genus `0`.**
99	
100	`degAff` is *defined* by reading the relative degree on a finite separable field refinement of
101	the class's own cover (`PicEtAff.degAff_mk`), which is exactly where the field layer
102	`relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero_of_genus_zero` applies.  Transport back to the original
103	cover is free — `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap` — so no comparison between covers is needed.
104	
105	**No curve section over `K` is required**, and hence no rational point: the landed plus-unit
106	surjectivity `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section` is not used, because the argument works on
107	the representative's own cover carrier rather than asking the class to come from `relPic`. -/
108	theorem eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero
109	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (hg : genus C = 0)
110	    (q : PicEtAff C K) (hq : PicEtAff.degAff (C := C) K q = 0) : q = 1 := by
111	  induction q using PicEtAff.ind with
112	  | mk E x =>
113	    obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLfin, hLsep, ⟨j⟩⟩ := E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
114	    letI := hLf; letI := hLa; letI := hLfin; letI := hLsep
115	    letI : Algebra k L := ((algebraMap K L).comp (algebraMap k K)).toAlgebra
116	    haveI : IsScalarTower k K L := IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
117	    -- the degree is the relative degree of the transported representative over `L`
118	    have hdeg : relPicDeg (C := C) L (relPicAlgMap C (j.restrictScalars k)
119	        (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) = 0 := by
120	      rw [← PicEtAff.degAff_mk (C := C) (K := K) E x L j]
121	      exact hq
122	    have htriv : relPicAlgMap C (j.restrictScalars k)
123	        (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) = 1 :=
124	      relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero_of_genus_zero C L hg _ hdeg
125	    -- transport to the field cover does not change the plus class
126	    have hstep : PicEtAff.mk C (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L)
127	        (descentMap C ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.comp j) x)
128	        = PicEtAff.mk C E x := PicEtAff.mk_descentMap C _ x
129	    rw [← hstep]
130	    convert PicEtAff.mk_one C (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L) using 2
131	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
132	    rw [descentMap_coe]
133	    have hcomp :
134	        ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.comp j).restrictScalars k
135	          = ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.restrictScalars k).comp
136	            (j.restrictScalars k) := rfl
137	    rw [hcomp, relPicAlgMap_comp, htriv, map_one]
138	    rfl
139	
140	-- Same instance stack, plus the affine comparison.
141	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
142	/-- **THE FIELD-TEST VANISHING**: at `genus C = 0`, the degree-zero Picard group of the curve
143	vanishes at every affine test over a *field*.
144	
145	Only **one** field point of the test is consulted — the identity `𝟙 (overSpec k K)`, at which
146	`degAt` is `degAff` of the class by `picEtMap_id`.  So the `∀ K, ∀ t` binder of
147	`pic0Subgroup`'s membership is used at a single instantiation, and the remaining field points
148	carry no weight in this direction. -/
149	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero
150	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (hg : genus C = 0) :
151	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K)) := by
152	  refine ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext ?_⟩
153	  refine (picEtAffineEquiv C K).injective ?_
154	  have hs : PicEtAff.degAff (C := C) K (picEtAffineEquiv C K s.1) = 0 := by
155	    have h := s.2 K (𝟙 (overSpec k K))
156	    rwa [degAt, picEtMap_id] at h
157	  have ht : PicEtAff.degAff (C := C) K (picEtAffineEquiv C K t.1) = 0 := by
158	    have h := t.2 K (𝟙 (overSpec k K))
159	    rwa [degAt, picEtMap_id] at h
160	  have h1 := eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero C K hg (picEtAffineEquiv C K s.1) hs
161	  have h2 := eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero C K hg (picEtAffineEquiv C K t.1) ht
162	  exact h1.trans h2.symm
163	
164	/-! ## Non-vacuity: the statement fires at a curve, unconditionally -/
165	
166	/-- **The field-test vanishing at `ℙ¹`, with no hypothesis.**
167	
168	`Curve/P1Curve.lean` gives `P1.asOver k` the three curve binders over an arbitrary field and
169	`Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` gives `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0`, so the theorem above applies with
170	nothing left to discharge.  Recorded because a conditional statement whose antecedent has no
171	witness is worth exactly nothing, and this one has one. -/
172	theorem P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field
173	    (k : Type u) [Field k] (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
174	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k K)) :=
175	  subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero (P1.asOver k) K
176	    (P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k)
177	
178	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.RigidEngine4Relative
7	
8	/-!
9	# RE-4 — the rigid engine fired on the relative twisted sheaf
10	
11	The Layer-2 keystones of the sheaf-level rigid engine (worksheet
12	`informal/w4-rigid-engine-worksheet.md` §1.2 Level 2): the abstract engine of
13	`RigidEngine4Assembly` instantiated on the **relative twisted sheaf**
14	`relTwistSheaf C R (fiberTwoCover π) g` on the pinned relative cover, with **every**
15	hypothesis discharged from the landed inputs:
16	
17	* the pair data (`relTwistPairData`) from the relative chart coordinates
18	  (`relFiberCoord₀/₁`, `RigidEngine4Relative`) through the generic twisted pair data
19	  (`twistPairData`, `RigidEngine4Twist`);
20	* the pinned `AEval'` chart finiteness through the trivializations and the relative E-i
21	  (`moduleFinite_aeval'_relTwistPair_t₀/₁`, = RE-4b assembled);
22	* flatness/projectivity of the section modules from freeness (`k`-bases are `R`-bases:
23	  `free_relSections` + `free_twistSheafSections₀/₁`).
24	
25	## Main declarations
26	
27	* `relTwistRigidEngine` — **Kleiman 3.10 (v)⟹(i)+(iii), curve-lite, relative**: under
28	  the complex-form fibrewise-vanishing hypothesis, `H¹(C_R, F_g) = 0` and
29	  `H⁰(C_R, F_g)` is a finite projective `R`-module.
30	* `relTwistRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` — the strata openness export.
31	* `relTwistH0TensorEquiv` — the module-coefficient clause (Kleiman `eq:Q`):
32	  `H⁰(C_R, F_g) ⊗[R] P ≃ₗ[R] ker (δ ⊗ P)` for every `R`-module `P`.
33	* `relTwistH0BaseChangeEquiv` — the ring-map clause, abstract half:
34	  `R' ⊗[R] H⁰(C_R, F_g) ≃ₗ[R'] ker (δ.baseChange R')` for every `R`-algebra `R'`
35	  (threading through CBC-1 onto `H⁰` of the base-changed sheaf composes this with
36	  `RigidEngine.kerCongr` along `relTwistTermBaseChange₀/₁`/`relTwistOverlapBaseChange`
37	  and the twisted δ-naturality — the `RelativeH1BaseChange` frontier).
38	
39	**Staging note (worksheet §3.2, BINDING).** The fibre hypothesis `hfib` is consumed in
40	COMPLEX form (`Subsingleton (H¹(pair) ⊗ κ(p))`); its sheaf-level discharge (glued fibre
41	sheaf ≅ divisor sheaf of a witness + the FLV class form) and the rank export
42	(`finrank κ(p) (H⁰ ⊗ κ(p)) = deg + χ`) gate on the W6-full seam and are deliberately NOT
43	attempted here.
44	-/
45

47	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
